# H3 Image Models

- [Comfy-Org MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image/tree/main): `minimax_h3_image_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors` (diffusion_models), `minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors` (vae), `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors` or `..._int8_convrot` (text_encoders)

## Text Encoder · Prompt Character Details

- [Qwen3.5-VL 9B w4a8 gptq](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image/blob/main/text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq.safetensors)

## Notes

- H3 Image is distilled: **6 steps, CFG 1** (the official ComfyUI template's settings), no sigma shift and no turbo LoRA.
- The video LoRAs of v1.1 (character swap, turbo, upscale) are for the video model; the LoRA slot here is for an H3 **Image** LoRA and is bypassed.
- The model works best at about 4 MP: the planner's *native* size keeps the short edge between 1024 and 2048.

nodes.title: Important Note
widgets_values:
> BFS Image Planner · the Shot Planner for one image
>
> The image is **<Picture 1>**, the picture MiniMax H3 Image edits; the references are <Picture 2>, <Picture 3>... Pick or drop the image in the 🖼 Image tab, the references and the prompt in 📝 Pictures & prompt, and what changes in ✏ Edit (SAM 3 selection, Full frame / Frame + paste / Mask only / Crop / Crop + mask, Colored Mark, {target}).
>
> The prompt node connected to the planner's prompt input wins over the panel's prompt (as in v1.1); disconnect it to use the panel's. {details} is the first reference's description (📝 Describe pictures, or the Prompt Enhancer CLIP at run time).
>
> The references go through BiRefNet (background removed) and Resize before the conditioning, as in v1.1; bypass both to use them as they are.

widgets_values_named.text:
> BFS Shot Planner — Optional
  >
  > This node was designed to simplify processing longer videos by splitting them into smaller shots. It also provides tools for prompt generation, subject segmentation, masks, cropping, uncropping, reference descriptions, and shot-by-shot
  > configuration.
  >
  > The planner is optional. If you prefer, you can use ComfyUI’s native Load Video nodes and limit the input to a maximum of 15 seconds, using a frame count supported by the model. In that setup, pass the input video through Add Guide instead
  > of the conventional native reference-video conditioning. The body or character reference should still be supplied as an image through the native reference node.
  >
  > One of the planner’s main advantages is its automatic loop: a single workflow run processes every configured shot and performs the swap sequentially. You can also configure the continuity/history window, which passes extra frames from the
  > previous generated shot into the next one to improve motion and visual continuity.
  >
  > Some variation between shots is still expected. This is especially noticeable when the character reference shows only part of the body, because the model may generate unseen clothing or body details differently in each shot. A clear full-
  > body reference generally improves consistency.
  >
  > You can review and edit the character description extracted from the reference image. This also allows you to request details that are not visible in the original reference, such as roller shoes, accessories, clothing changes, or other
  > character features. This feature is still experimental and has not been explored extensively.

| 1024-2048 | kept |

widgets_values: subject_definitions: <Subject 1> is the {details} shown in <Picture 2>, whose identity, face, head, hair or fur, skin, body shape, proportions and clothing define the character in the result. <Picture 1> is the image to edit: it provides the scene, background, environment, lighting, camera, framing, body pose, hand and arm position, head orientation, gaze direction and facial expression; only the main subject of <Picture 1> is replaced: its face, hair, body and clothing become <Subject 1>.  summary: [image editing + reference generation] Replace the main subject of <Picture 1> with <Subject 1>, keeping the scene, camera, pose and expression of <Picture 1>.  retention_analysis: <Subject 1> takes the exact place, pose and expression of the original subject while keeping the complete identity from <Picture 2>: facial structure, hair or fur, skin, body shape and clothing. The background, lighting, colors, camera and framing of <Picture 1>: fully_preserved.

widgets_values_named.value: body_swap: subject_definitions: <Subject 1> is the {details} shown in <Picture 1>, whose identity, face, head, hair or fur, skin, body shape, proportions and clothing define the character in the target video. The guide video provides the scene and the performance: its background, environment, lighting, camera, framing, body pose, hand and arm movement, head rotation, gaze direction, lip movement and facial expression, frame by frame; only the main subject of the guide video is replaced: its face, hair, body and clothing become <Subject 1>.  summary: [video generation + reference] Replace the guide subject with <Subject 1>, keeping the scene, camera and the complete motion and performance of the guide video.  detailed_description: [Shot 1] <Subject 1> takes the exact place of the guide subject and moves with the same timing, body pose, gestures, head motion, gaze, speech and facial expressions, while keeping the complete identity from <Picture 1>: facial structure, hair or fur, skin, body shape and clothing stay stable in every frame. The background, lighting, colors and camera of the guide video are preserved. Prevent identity drift, clothing changes, texture crawling and flicker.
